- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.5), model tends to underpredict prices; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% to counteract pessimism.
- After a price spike (e.g., >70), model often overreacts and overshoots in next 3–5 days; cap forecast at +10% above peak or use 2-day moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment is positive (especially > 0.3), model frequently overestimates; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% to avoid overconfidence.
- Mean reversion is strong in 10–14 day horizon; if forecast is >1.5σ above recent mean, reduce by 0.3–0.7σ to align with historical volatility.
- Model underperforms in early horizon (1–3 days) when sentiment is volatile; use 3-day weighted average of recent history to anchor short-term forecast.
- If sentiment turns sharply positive after a negative streak, model often misses the rebound; add 0.2–0.5% buffer to forecast for sentiment reversal.
